title: Evaluating a text and supporting your view
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Reading is not only about understanding — it is about judging. When you evaluate a text, you give your own view and back it up with evidence from the text.
To support an opinion about a text, give evidence FROM the text — not just a feeling.

steps: Strong support: 'Because she ran into the burning house to save the cat.'

blocks.question: What is the best way to support your view about a text?
blocks.explain: A strong view is backed by evidence taken from the text itself.
blocks.rule: Support your opinion about a text with evidence from the text.

practiceItems.prompt: back up your opinion with ___ from the text
'because she saved the cat' is an example of ___

blocks.content: To evaluate is to judge how good, useful or convincing a text is — and say why.

blocks.question: When you evaluate a text, you are:
options: judging how good or convincing it is
blocks.explain: Evaluating means judging the quality of a text and giving reasons.
blocks.rule: To evaluate a text is to judge how good, useful or convincing it is, with reasons.

practiceItems.prompt: to evaluate a text is to ___ it (judge/copy)
a judgement should be backed with ___
your view of a text is your ___
evidence for your view comes from the ___

blocks.content: Give your view, then prove it with evidence from the text. That is how you evaluate well. Let's practise!
